officialDocs.label: Create or refresh an access token (scopes)

verdict.summary: There's no app review, but PandaDoc's plan table marks Applications/OAuth as unavailable on Free and Starter, included in the API Developer Plan, and a paid add-on on Business and Enterprise, so you need to pay before you can even create an OAuth app. Once you have it, the flow is simple: two scopes (read, write) and access tokens that last about a year.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Assumes you buy the API Developer Plan self-serve. If you're on Business/Enterprise and need the OAuth add-on through sales, add days. API keys (sandbox) work sooner, but they aren't OAuth.

timeToProd.assumes: You're on a plan that includes OAuth applications (API Developer Plan) and your agent reads and writes documents in users' own PandaDoc workspaces.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing — no review. The only gate is the paid plan or add-on (and sales, if you go the add-on route).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: None of the PandaDoc pages we read mention an app review or marketplace approval for OAuth apps. That doesn't rule out terms-of-use checks.

verdict.cost: API Developer Plan, $40/month including 40 documents sent per month and $4 per extra document; or a paid OAuth add-on on Business/Enterprise (contact sales).

prerequisites.item: A PandaDoc plan that includes Applications/OAuth
prerequisites.why: The plan table marks Applications/OAuth as unavailable on Free and Starter, included on the API Developer Plan, and a paid add-on on Business and Enterprise.

prerequisites.item: Account owner or admin role, with the Dev Center enabled
prerequisites.why: Only the owner and admin-role users can open the Dev Center, which is enabled under Settings > API and Integrations > API.

prerequisites.item: A verified email and production API access
prerequisites.why: The OAuth guide says application creation is only available with production API access enabled; the sandbox key is for testing the public API.

prerequisites.item: A redirect URL that matches the app settings exactly
prerequisites.why: redirect_uri in the authorize request has to match the application settings.

scopeTiers.impact: View templates and document details. Enough for an agent that summarizes or tracks document status.
Create, send, delete and download documents. Most agents that generate or send documents need this. 'read+write' is deprecated; send 'read write' (space-separated).

steps.title: Get a plan that includes OAuth applications
steps.detail: Subscribe to the API Developer Plan, or ask sales for the Applications/OAuth add-on on Business or Enterprise.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Self-serve vs sales timing is our estimate.

steps.title: Enable the Dev Center
steps.detail: As account owner or admin, go to Settings > API and Integrations > API and click Enable.

steps.title: Draft the application details
steps.detail: Prepare the application name, publisher, redirect URL, description, support email and app website.

steps.title: Create the application
steps.detail: Dev Center > Configuration > Create application. Fill in the fields, agree to the PandaDoc API terms of use, and copy the generated client_id and client_secret.

steps.title: Implement the authorize redirect
steps.detail: Send users to https://app.pandadoc.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=read+write&response_type=code (encode the space in 'read write'). PandaDoc redirects back with ?code=.

steps.title: Exchange the code and store tokens
steps.detail: POST form-encoded grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret and code to https://api.pandadoc.com/oauth2/access_token. Store access_token and refresh_token per user.

steps.title: Handle 401 with a refresh
steps.detail: On 401 Unauthorized, POST grant_type=refresh_token with the stored refresh token. On invalid_grant, send the user back through authorization.

steps.title: Test with a second PandaDoc account
steps.detail: Sign in as a different PandaDoc user and connect through your app to confirm it works outside your own workspace and on the end user's plan.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: We couldn't confirm whether end users on Free or Starter can authorize a third-party OAuth app; testing this is the point of the step.

steps.title: Add 429 backoff
steps.detail: Respect per-user, per-endpoint limits (for example 100 RPM on Download Document) and back off on 429.

agentCanDo: Draft the application name, description and redirect URL
Implement the authorize, token exchange and refresh flow
Build per-endpoint rate limiting and 429 backoff
Check the authorize and token endpoints respond
humanMustDo: Pay for the API Developer Plan or OAuth add-on
Enable the Dev Center as account owner or admin
Create the application and accept the API terms of use
Test the connection from a second PandaDoc account

blockers.symptom: No 'Create application' option, or no Dev Center under Settings
blockers.cause: Your plan doesn't include Applications/OAuth (Free and Starter don't), or you're not the owner/admin, or the Dev Center isn't enabled.
blockers.fix: Upgrade to the API Developer Plan or buy the add-on, then enable the Dev Center as owner/admin.

blockers.cause: grant_type missing, or the body was sent as JSON instead of form-encoded.
blockers.fix: Send Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded with grant_type=authorization_code (or refresh_token).

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: An empty POST to api.pandadoc.com/oauth2/access_token returned this on 2026-10-20.

blockers.cause: The refresh token is invalid, for example because a newer token pair was generated and invalidated the old one.
blockers.fix: Re-run authorization. Avoid generating parallel token pairs for the same user.

blockers.cause: You exceeded a per-user, per-endpoint limit over the 60-second sliding window (10 RPM on any sandbox endpoint).
blockers.fix: Back off and spread calls. Limits are per user, so each connected user has their own budget.

blockers.symptom: Document creation errors after a while in production
blockers.cause: Production API calls consume usage credits, and creation can fail once credits run out.
blockers.fix: Monitor credit usage and buy more volume; budget $4 per extra document on the Developer Plan.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Which account's credits an OAuth call consumes (yours or the end user's) wasn't stated.

nuances.text: Access tokens currently last 31,535,999 seconds (about one year). The refresh token lifetime and whether it rotates aren't documented.
Generating a new token invalidates the old one, and each access/refresh pair needs a fresh authorization code.
Rate limits apply to production and OAuth keys per user, not per key, and vary by endpoint (for example 600 RPM for document details, 100 RPM for downloads). Sandbox keys get 10 RPM on any endpoint.

PandaDoc's plan lineup changed in 2026: the Free plan gained API access around June 2026, but the plan table still excludes Applications/OAuth on Free and Starter, so an API key works where OAuth doesn't.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The June 2026 date comes from search-result summaries of a PandaDoc blog post we couldn't open (HTTP 429). The plan table (s3) shows a Free column with API features but no OAuth.

nuances.text: Request bodies are capped at 2 MB and PDF uploads at 50 MB (413 if larger).
